content: International Emergency Medicine is a specialized field that examines the current standards and advancements in emergency medical care across various countries worldwide. In the United States, Emergency Medicine has been recognized as a distinct medical specialty for over two decades. The term International Emergency Medicine typically refers to the process of transferring expertise, skills, and knowledge from well-established emergency medical systems to those in less developed regions. This includes sharing knowledge about ambulance operations and pre-hospital care systems. In many developing nations, efforts are underway to establish Emergency Medicine as a formal specialty. These efforts include creating accreditation systems and promoting the development of training programs in emergency medicine. International Emergency Medicine (IEM) is considered a sub-specialty within the broader field of emergency medicine. In the United States, several fellowship programs in International Emergency Medicine are available. These fellowships provide residency-trained emergency physicians with advanced training in global health, international systems development, and related skills. Many of these programs also offer fellows the opportunity to earn an advanced degree, such as a Master of Public Health (MPH). The following institutions in the United States offer International Emergency Medicine Fellowships: Alameda County Medical Center Highland Hospital Loma Linda University Keck School of Medicine at the University of Southern California George Washington University Emory University Medical College of Georgia Rush University/Cook County Hospital University of Illinois at Chicago The Johns Hopkins University University of Maryland Bellevue Hospital Center/New York University Columbia University/New York Presbyterian Hospital Long Island Jewish Medical Center University of Rochester Medical Center University of Pittsburgh Rhode Island Hospital Brown University The International Conference on Emergency Medicine (ICEM) is a biennial event that brings together emergency physicians from around the world. This conference is organized by the International Federation for Emergency Medicine (IFEM), which was originally founded by four national emergency physician organizations: the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), the British Association for Emergency Medicine (BAEM), the Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians (CAEP), and the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM). Historically, the conference has rotated among these founding member organizations. However, in recent years, new member organizations have joined IFEM, and the conference is now scheduled to rotate among these newer members as well.
